title: "Solution: Model Building in Practice — Diamonds, Flights, and Growth Models"
output: html_document

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(modelr)
library(broom)
library(nycflights13)
```

```{r load-data}
data("diamonds", package = "ggplot2")
data("flights",  package = "nycflights13")
```

## Task 1: Progressive diamond model — step by step

```{r task1a}
mod1 <- lm(price ~ carat, data = diamonds)
summary(mod1)
# R² ≈ 0.85 — looks good at first glance.

diamonds |>
  add_residuals(mod1) |>
  ggplot(aes(carat, resid, colour = cut)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title    = "Model 1 residuals: price ~ carat",
    subtitle = "Fan shape (heteroscedasticity) and cut clusters are clearly visible",
    x        = "carat", y = "Residual"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Problem 1: fan shape — variance grows with carat (heteroscedasticity).
# Problem 2: residuals cluster by cut and colour — those variables explain
#            remaining variation that carat alone cannot capture.
```

```{r task1b}
mod2 <- lm(log(price) ~ log(carat), data = diamonds)
summary(mod2)
# R² rises to ≈ 0.93 after the log-log transformation.

diamonds |>
  add_residuals(mod2) |>
  ggplot(aes(log(carat), resid, colour = cut)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title    = "Model 2 residuals: log(price) ~ log(carat)",
    subtitle = "Fan shape gone, but cut clusters remain — cut must enter the model",
    x        = "log(carat)", y = "Residual"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# The fan shape is gone — the log-log transform linearises the power-law
# relationship and stabilises variance.  However, systematic bands by cut
# remain; the model still misses the quality dimension.
```

```{r task1c}
mod3 <- lm(log(price) ~ log(carat) + cut + colour + clarity, data = diamonds)
summary(mod3)
# R² ≈ 0.98 — near-perfect after absorbing the quality variables.

diamonds |>
  add_residuals(mod3) |>
  ggplot(aes(log(carat), resid, colour = cut)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title    = "Model 3 residuals: log(price) ~ log(carat) + cut + colour + clarity",
    subtitle = "Residuals are now random — no systematic pattern remains",
    x        = "log(carat)", y = "Residual"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Residuals scatter randomly around zero with no visible banding.
# This is the stopping criterion: residuals look like noise.
```

## Task 2: Many-models pipeline — flights by carrier

```{r task2}
carrier_models <- flights |>
  drop_na(arr_delay, dep_delay) |>
  group_by(carrier) |>
  nest() |>
  mutate(
    model = map(data,  ~lm(arr_delay ~ dep_delay, data = .x)),
    coefs = map(model, broom::tidy)
  ) |>
  unnest(coefs)

dep_delay_slopes <- carrier_models |>
  filter(term == "dep_delay") |>
  select(carrier, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value) |>
  arrange(estimate)

print(dep_delay_slopes)

# Interpretation: carriers with slope < 1 make up time in the air on average;
# carriers with slope > 1 fall further behind for each extra minute delayed.
```

```{r task2-plot}
dep_delay_slopes |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(carrier, estimate), y = estimate)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(estimate, 2)), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.2) +
  labs(
    title    = "dep_delay slope by carrier: lm(arr_delay ~ dep_delay)",
    subtitle = "Dashed line at slope = 1.  Below: carrier makes up time.  Above: carrier falls further behind.",
    x        = "Carrier",
    y        = "Slope estimate (minutes of arr_delay per minute of dep_delay)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Task 3: Non-linear growth model with nls()

```{r task3-data}
set.seed(602)

K  <- 1000
r  <- 0.4
Y0 <- 50

t  <- seq(0, 20, by = 1)
Y  <- K / (1 + ((K - Y0) / Y0) * exp(-r * t)) + rnorm(length(t), sd = 20)
growth_df <- tibble(t = t, Y = pmax(Y, 0))

ggplot(growth_df, aes(t, Y)) +
  geom_point(colour = "steelblue", size = 2.5) +
  labs(title = "Simulated logistic growth data",
       x = "Time", y = "Population") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r task3-fit}
mod_nls <- nls(
  Y ~ K / (1 + ((K - Y0) / Y0) * exp(-r * t)),
  data  = growth_df,
  start = list(K = 900, r = 0.5, Y0 = 60)
)

summary(mod_nls)

K_hat  <- coef(mod_nls)["K"]
r_hat  <- coef(mod_nls)["r"]
Y0_hat <- coef(mod_nls)["Y0"]

cat(sprintf("Estimated K  (carrying capacity): %.1f  (true: 1000)\n", K_hat))
cat(sprintf("Estimated r  (growth rate):       %.3f (true: 0.400)\n", r_hat))
cat(sprintf("Estimated Y0 (initial population):%.1f  (true: 50)\n",   Y0_hat))
```

```{r task3-plot}
growth_df |>
  add_predictions(mod_nls) |>
  ggplot(aes(t)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = Y), colour = "steelblue", size = 2.5) +
  geom_line(aes(y = pred), colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 1.2) +
  annotate("text", x = 3, y = K_hat * 0.95,
           label = sprintf("Estimated K = %.0f", K_hat),
           colour = "firebrick", hjust = 0, size = 4) +
  labs(
    title    = "Logistic growth: observed vs nls() fitted curve",
    subtitle = "Red curve is the fitted logistic; blue points are simulated observations",
    x        = "Time", y = "Population"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Task 4: Residual diagnostics across all three models

```{r task4}
# --- Model 1: price ~ carat ---
p1 <- diamonds |>
  add_residuals(mod1) |>
  mutate(fitted = fitted(mod1)) |>
  ggplot(aes(fitted, resid)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 0.5, colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  labs(title = "Model 1: price ~ carat",
       subtitle = "Fan shape (heteroscedasticity)",
       x = "Fitted values", y = "Residuals") +
  theme_minimal()

# --- Model 3: log(price) ~ log(carat) + cut + colour + clarity ---
p3 <- diamonds |>
  add_residuals(mod3) |>
  mutate(fitted = fitted(mod3)) |>
  ggplot(aes(fitted, resid)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 0.5, colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  labs(title = "Model 3: log(price) ~ log(carat) + cut + colour + clarity",
       subtitle = "Random scatter — residuals look like noise",
       x = "Fitted values", y = "Residuals") +
  theme_minimal()

# --- Non-linear model: logistic growth ---
p_nls <- tibble(
  fitted = fitted(mod_nls),
  resid  = residuals(mod_nls)
) |>
  ggplot(aes(fitted, resid)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  labs(title = "NLS logistic growth model",
       subtitle = "No systematic pattern — nls() converged well",
       x = "Fitted values", y = "Residuals") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p1)
print(p3)
print(p_nls)

# Summary:
# Model 1 shows a pronounced fan shape — variance grows with fitted values.
# Model 3 shows random scatter — the progressive additions absorbed all structure.
# The NLS residuals show no pattern — the logistic curve fits the simulated data well.
```
